result.topic_en: Euler finishes classifying the residues a for prime divisors of numbers of the form pp+39qq into classes I and III and lists those prime divisors up to 312; Corollary 1 then explains why the second class reduces to the first.

Nunc igitur omnes numeri primi in forma $156i+a$ contenti certe erunt diuiſores cuiuſpiam numeri formae $pp+39qq$, atque adeo vel ipſi, vel eorum quintupla, vel etiam tripla erunt numeri huius formae. Hinc ergo omnes diuiſores primi ab $1$ vsque ad $312$ erunt ſequentes:
$1, 5, 11, 41, 43, 47, 59, 61, 71, 79, 83, 89, 113, 127, 137, 139, 149, 157, 167, 181, 197, 199, 211, 227, 239, 269, 277, 281, 283, 293.$

Corollarium 1.

§. 44. Quo facilius intelligatur, cur hoc caſu claſſis ſecunda ad primam ſit reuoluta, iam ſupra oſtendimus, ſi diuiſor fuerit
$D=frr+2grs+hss,$
exiſtente $fh=gg+n$, tum non ſolum $Df$, ſed etiam $Dh$ ad formam $pp+nqq$ reduci poſſe. Hinc autem generalius ſi fuerit
$k=ftt+2gtu+huu,$
tum productum $Dk$ etiam erit numerus formae $pp+nqq$; facto enim calculo reperitur
$Dk=(frt+g(ts+ru)+hsu)^2+n(ts-ru)^2.$
Quod ſi ergo $k$ fieri queat quadratum, vel diuiſibile per quadratum, tum hoc quadratum omitti poterit. Nam ſi fuerit $Dkll$ numerus formae $pp+nqq$, tum, etiam admiſſis fractionibus, erit quoque $Dk$ eiusdem formae. Ita noſtro caſu pro diuiſoribus ſecundae claſſis erat
$D=3rr+13ss,$
ideoque $k=3tt+13uu$, cuius valor ſumto $t=1$ et $u=1$ fiet $k=16$, qui cum ſit numerus quadratus, haec forma ad primam reducitur.

items.quote: Hoc modo omnes noſtri numeri ſigna ſua debita ſunt adepti, qui cum vel ad primam vel ad tertiam claſſem referantur, manifeſtum eſt nullos diuiſores ſecundae claſſis relinqui.
items.english: In this way all our numbers have obtained their proper signs; and since they belong either to the first or to the third class, it is evident that no divisors of the second class remain.

items.quote: Nunc igitur omnes numeri primi in forma $156i+a$ contenti certe erunt diuiſores cuiuſpiam numeri formae $pp+39qq$, atque adeo vel ipſi, vel eorum quintupla, vel etiam tripla erunt numeri huius formae.
items.english: Now therefore all prime numbers contained in the form 156i+a will certainly be divisors of some number of the form pp+39qq, and so either they themselves, or their quintuples, or their triples will be numbers of this form.

$k=ftt+2gtu+huu,$
tum productum $Dk$ etiam erit numerus formae $pp+nqq$
items.english: If k = ftt+2gtu+huu, then the product Dk will also be a number of the form pp+nqq.

items.quote: Nam ſi fuerit $Dkll$ numerus formae $pp+nqq$, tum, etiam admiſſis fractionibus, erit quoque $Dk$ eiusdem formae.
items.english: For if Dkll is a number of the form pp+nqq, then, admitting fractions as well, Dk will also be of the same form.

items.quote: Quo facilius intelligatur, cur hoc caſu claſſis ſecunda ad primam ſit reuoluta
items.english: So that it may be understood more easily why in this case the second class has been reduced to the first.
